record.paper_title: A common approach to three open problems in number theory
record.context_brief: Hypothesis 1 on bounded finite-solution subsystems of A
record.original_question: Let A be the set of all equations of the forms x_i · x_j = x_k for i, j, k ∈ {1, ..., 7} together with 2^(2^(x_j)) = x_k for j, k ∈ {1, ..., 7}. If a subsystem S ⊆ A has at most five equations and only finitely many solutions in (ℕ \ {0, 1})^7, must every such solution (x_1, ..., x_7) satisfy x_1, ..., x_7 ≤ 16?

evidence.quote: Hypothesis 1. If a system of equations S ⊆ A has at most five equations and at most finitely many solutions in (N \ {0, 1})^7, then each such solution (x1, . . . , x7) satisfies x1, . . . , x7 6 16.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N}=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ and let $A$ denote the set of equations in the unknowns $x_1,\ldots,x_7$ consisting of all equations of the form
\[ x_i\cdot x_j = x_k,\qquad i,j,k\in\{1,\ldots,7\}, \]
together with all equations of the form
\[ 2^{2^{x_j}} = x_k,\qquad j,k\in\{1,\ldots,7\}. \]
Decide whether the following statement holds: for every subsystem $S\subseteq A$ that contains at most five equations and has only finitely many solutions $(x_1,\ldots,x_7)\in(\mathbb{N}\setminus\{0,1\})^7$, every such solution satisfies $x_i\le 16$ for all $i\in\{1,\ldots,7\}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is formulated as a hypothesis (conjecture) by Tyszka in work on Diophantine systems related to open problems in number theory; subsequent versions of his papers continue to list it as a hypothesis without proof. No published resolution was located.

status_evidence.snippet: References Hypothesis 1 in the form of a conjecture about subsystems of A with at most finitely many solutions in (N\{0,1})^7.
status_evidence.claim: The statement is presented as an unproven hypothesis in Tyszka's writings.
